criteria.title: Hangfire Infrastructure, Dashboard Protection, and Retries
criteria.description: Hangfire is configured with the free packages only (Hangfire.Core, Hangfire.AspNetCore, and Hangfire.SqlServer) with persistent UseSqlServerStorage on SQL Server, and AddHangfireServer registered in Program.cs. JOB-05: The /hangfire dashboard cannot be opened without logging in (an anonymous request returns 401), and is protected by basic authentication using credentials from HangfireDashboardOptions validated with ValidateOnStart and sourced from user-secrets or environment variables (or a policy requiring the Admin role), not by the default LocalRequestsOnly filter. NTF-04: Every job is automatically retried at least 3 times (AutomaticRetry with Attempts = 3 or a global filter), and each failed attempt is logged at Error level (verifiable by having a job throw an exception and observing the dashboard and logs).

criteria.title: Email Service via MailKit and Mailpit
criteria.description: NTF-01: The IEmailService interface is defined in DonationHub.Application and implemented in DonationHub.Infrastructure using MailKit and MimeKit, with SMTP settings from EmailOptions (Host, Port, SenderEmail, and SenderName), and credentials from user-secrets or environment variables only. NTF-06: In Development, emails go to Mailpit on localhost:1025 and no real email is sent. NTF-02 and NTF-03: The receipt email reaches the donor with an attached PDF file, and the goal-reached email reaches the campaign creator; both appear in the Mailpit dashboard at http://localhost:8025. NTF-05: Email text uses the recipient's PreferredLanguage (ar or en), and Arabic emails use <html dir="rtl" lang="ar"> and render right-to-left. SMTP exceptions are not swallowed so that Hangfire retries the job.

criteria.title: PDF Receipt via QuestPDF and Protected Download
criteria.description: QuestPDF is configured with QuestPDF.Settings.License = LicenseType.Community in Program.cs. FIL-06: The receipt is generated inside a Hangfire job rather than inside the HTTP request, in the donor's language, and contains the receipt number formatted as DN-{year}-{6-digit sequence}, transaction date, campaign title in the donor's language, category, donor name, formatted amount with currency, and organization verification header and footer; Arabic text renders with a proper font and right-to-left direction. The file is stored through IFileStorage outside any public folder. FIL-07: GET /donations/{id}/receipt returns an application/pdf file to the donation owner or an Admin only; another user's donation returns 404, and an unauthenticated request without a token returns 401.

criteria.title: Secure Campaign Banner Upload and Magic Bytes Validation
criteria.description: FIL-01: POST /campaigns/{id}/banner accepts an IFormFile in multipart/form-data format only from an Admin or the Campaign Manager who owns the campaign (a non-owner receives 404); allowed types are JPG, PNG, and WEBP with a maximum size of 2 MB configurable via FileStorageOptions. FIL-02: File type is determined by inspecting the initial raw bytes (FF D8 FF, PNG, and RIFF....WEBP) rather than the extension or ContentType; an .exe file renamed to .jpg is rejected with File.InvalidType (400), and a file exceeding the limit returns File.TooLarge (413) in ProblemDetails format. FIL-03: Storage goes through IFileStorage (interface in Application and disk implementation in Infrastructure) using a random Guid name rather than the user's file name. FIL-04: Replacing the banner deletes the old file, DELETE /campaigns/{id}/banner works with the same permissions, and soft-deleting a campaign retains the file. FIL-05: The campaign response includes bannerUrl, which serves the image publicly.

criteria.title: Jobs: Post-Commit Enqueueing and Scheduling
criteria.description: Jobs are enqueued only after the success-flow transaction (DON-07) commits successfully and never inside or before it, and the POST /admin/donations/{id}/mark-succeeded stub triggers the same flow. JOB-01 (Fire-and-forget) generates the receipt and emails it to the donor, and JOB-02 is enqueued only if the campaign has just become Completed. JOB-03 (DON-09): On POST /campaigns/{campaignId}/donations, a delayed job is scheduled after DonationOptions.PendingTimeoutMinutes (30 minutes by default) to mark the donation as Failed if it is still Pending, and do nothing otherwise. JOB-04: An hourly recurring job (Cron.Hourly or 0 * * * *) transitions Active campaigns past their EndDate to Expired. Job arguments are IDs only (Guid), never entities or DbContext. No email or PDF work executes inside the HTTP request, and the donation response is fast (roughly under 100ms) because heavy work is queued.

criteria.title: Job Idempotency
criteria.description: Running the same job twice sends exactly one email and changes state only once: before executing, each job checks a persisted marker in the database or the current status—for example, the receipt job checks ReceiptSentAt and does not regenerate a new PDF on retry, the goal-reached job checks GoalEmailSentAt, the stale pending donation job checks that the donation is still Pending, and the expire-campaigns job finds nothing to update on the second run. This can be verified by re-triggering a succeeded job from the Hangfire dashboard and checking Mailpit.

criteria.title: Structured Logging with Serilog
criteria.description: Serilog (Serilog.AspNetCore) replaces the default logger with two primary sinks: Console and a daily rolling file (such as logs/donationhub-.log). UseSerilogRequestLogging is enabled and captures the status code and request duration. Every log entry is enriched with traceId and the user id when authenticated (both appearing in Console and the file). Messages use structured templates like "Donation {DonationId} succeeded" rather than string concatenation, and log levels are accurate: Information for business events, Warning for recoverable anomalies such as a late payment, and Error for failures including job attempts. Background job execution appears in the logs. No secrets are logged (passwords, JWT or refresh tokens, SMTP credentials, or card data).

criteria.title: Tests and Secret Protection
criteria.description: Unit tests cover the new behavior and pass with dotnet test: file signature validation (including rejecting an exe file with a jpg extension), stale pending donation job logic (Pending becomes Failed, and other statuses remain unchanged), and job idempotency. Time is obtained via TimeProvider rather than DateTime.UtcNow inside handlers and jobs. SMTP credentials and HangfireDashboardOptions credentials are absent from appsettings*.json and Git history, and are read from user-secrets or environment variables.

criteria.title: README and Submission
criteria.description: The README is updated for the sprint: what was added, how to try it (e.g., running Mailpit and configuring secrets, then donating and calling mark-succeeded, checking Mailpit and the /hangfire dashboard, and uploading a spoofed image), and key decisions (such as post-commit enqueueing and how idempotency is achieved). The sprint-4 tag exists and points to the final commit, and any fixes are tagged as sprint-4-fix without moving the original tag.

criteria.title: Explaining Decisions and Trade-offs
criteria.description: The learner's ability during review to explain their decisions, alternatives, and trade-offs, such as: what happens if the receipt job runs twice, or if SMTP fails after generating the PDF? Why is the job enqueued after the commit rather than before it, what could be lost, and how does the Outbox pattern solve it? Why do we pass only a Guid to the job? Why is checking the extension or ContentType insufficient? What happens if mark-succeeded arrives while JOB-03 is executing? Why use basic auth for the Hangfire dashboard and why doesn't JWT work from a browser? The difference between Fire-and-forget, Delayed, and Recurring jobs, and the difference between a structured template and string concatenation in Serilog. Answers are evaluated on understanding rather than memorization.
